Chapter 5: Obstacles to Spiritual Growth and the Call to Deeper Pursuit
When you set out on the path toward a deeper connection with God, you’ll quickly notice it’s not always a smooth road. There are real obstacles in the way—some you’ll see coming, and others that sneak up when you least expect them.
Think about it. Complacency, distraction, and the constant pull of the world—they can all work together, quietly, to keep your heart from chasing after the divine. The first step in moving forward is simply noticing these barriers for what they are.
Let’s talk about complacency for a moment. Out of all the obstacles, this one might be the trickiest. It slips in quietly, making you feel like things are “good enough.” Your faith becomes comfortable, almost routine, and that deep hunger for something more just fades away. Maybe you start to think that real spiritual growth is only for the especially devoted, or that a closer relationship with God is just out of reach for you. But here’s the truth: complacency is a thief. It steals the joy and excitement that come from truly encountering God.
Then there’s distraction. Our world is noisier than ever—demands, entertainment, endless scrolling. It’s so easy to get so busy that you have no space left for God. Sometimes, even good things like work, family, or helping others can crowd out those quiet moments your soul needs. Your heart gets pulled in so many directions, it’s hard to focus on what really matters.
Now, worldliness is a little more subtle. It’s not usually a dramatic shift, just a slow drift. Over time, you find yourself caring more about comfort, success, or what others think than about the things of God. It’s a series of small choices, little compromises, that add up without you even noticing.
For a lot of people, there’s a wake-up call—a moment when they’ve chased after success, approval, or pleasure, and end up feeling empty. The things that promised fulfillment just don’t deliver, and you’re left with a sense of hollowness. It’s in that emptiness the heart remembers its true hunger—the longing for God that only He can satisfy.
So, what’s the call here? It’s not about cramming more into your schedule or trying to be perfect. It’s about wanting more. It’s an invitation to come back to the source, to seek the God who’s always reaching out for you. This isn’t about earning approval or checking off spiritual boxes. It’s simply saying “yes” to the journey.
For some, that means creating space—setting aside time for silence, reflection, and prayer. For others, it might mean cutting back on distractions and choosing to focus on what truly matters. Sometimes, it takes making tough choices—saying no to some good things so you can say yes to what’s best.
Let’s be honest, the journey isn’t always easy. There will be setbacks, doubts, and dry seasons. But here’s something to hold onto: those who seek will find. If your heart truly longs for God, you won’t be disappointed.
